comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C52-C58. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the evidence for unconscious learning during sleep, based on feeling-of-having-heard measures and confidence ratings showing no awareness of sleep-presented stimuli.

Both address behavioral findings (C42, C45-C47) showing trough-targeted stimulation produces above-chance retrieval. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about statistical power. Peer reviewers accept the behavioral effect as 'solid evidence' but rate UNCERTAIN due to fundamental concerns about whether this represents true episodic memory versus perceptual associations.

Both address EEG findings on prototypical troughs (C68, C71-C74). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on cluster-based permutation tests. Peer reviewers also accept these findings as SUPPORTED, noting they 'offer hints to others on how to improve or predict the efficacy of this intervention.'

Both address spectral markers (C76-C79). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with note that spindle-behavior correlation is absent. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning the functional significance of spindles given the lack of differential effects on performance.

Both address ERP patterns (C60-C65, C125-C126). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting well-documented patterns with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also accept as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the authors provided 'solid arguments based on existing literature.'

Both address neural complexity findings (C88-C89, C95). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes interpretation is speculative and item-level effects are absent. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without challenging the complexity findings.

Both address memory consolidation over time (C107-C112). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about tagging and preferential consolidation lacks direct evidence. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN and explicitly challenge the dismissal of repeated testing effects as a confound.

Both address the integrative mechanistic model (C152-C154). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting it's explicitly speculative and serves as hypothesis-generating framework. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the speculative labeling but noting empirical gaps, particularly regarding spindle effects.

Both address methodological limitations (C170-C171). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of stimulus duration and complexity confounds. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as SUPPORTED, noting the authors provided solid arguments regarding these issues.

Both address episodic memory interpretation (C101-C103, C165, C22, C96). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, accepting the episodic memory framework with citations. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly challenging the 'episodic' terminology and recommending its removal from the title, arguing the evidence doesn't support this interpretation.

Both address arguments against simpler explanations (C106, C128). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for the logical argument against priming. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating this is 'an opinion, not a demonstration' and calling for control conditions to exclude perceptual association hypotheses.

Partial overlap on integrative model (C96). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to substantial speculation about mechanisms. Peer reviewers challenge the episodic memory interpretation more fundamentally, rating UNSUPPORTED and arguing the findings represent a distinct form of learning.

Minimal overlap (C128). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN regarding processing duration assumptions during sleep. Peer reviewers focus on challenging simpler associative explanations, rating the episodic interpretation as UNSUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap (C165). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for contextualization within unconscious memory literature, though notes theoretical implications are somewhat overstated. Peer reviewers fundamentally challenge the episodic memory framing, rating UNSUPPORTED.
OpenEval evaluates memory stability and improvement claims (C48-C51) as SUPPORTED but notes lack of formal significance tests. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates hippocampal theta interpretation (C137-C143) as UNCERTAIN, noting highly speculative mechanisms without direct hippocampal evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates spindle function claims (C144-C151) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of correlation between spindle power and behavior undermines functional interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates explanations for peak condition failure (C114-C124) as UNCERTAIN, noting post-hoc speculations about peaks being 'occupied' lack direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates methodological details (C34-C40, C177-C180) as SUPPORTED, noting sufficient detail for replication. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates potential confounds and their statistical assessment (C181-C188) as SUPPORTED, though notes inference based on absence of correlation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates comparison to prior work (C156-C163) as SUPPORTED, noting sound logic about timing differences and appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates speculative therapeutic applications (C173-C176) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are premature extrapolations given modest effect sizes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
